title: YEATS2/TAK1 axis mediates TGF-beta1 driven adaptive resistance to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Bai, Lizhi; Wang, Yu; Li, Guanyi; Song, Yi; Yu, Yongliang; Tang, Rongbin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究YEATS2/TAK1轴介导TGF-β1驱动的肝癌索拉非尼耐药，虽含结构建模和分子动力学模拟，但核心是蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法可部分借鉴。
abstract: Although Sorafenib can effectively prolong the median survival time of HCC patients with limited side effects, it may cause many patients to develop drug resistance, becoming a barrier to extending the overall survival time of HCC patients. Our previous research explored the mechanism of the TGF-beta1 pathway in the occurrence and development of liver cancer; the mechanism of the TGF-beta1 pathway in sorafenib resistance needs further exploration. Through the analysis of the related sequencing results of TGF-beta1-treated Huh7 cells and sorafenib-resistant Huh7 cells in the GEO database, we identified YEATS2 as a TGF-beta1-responsive gene that is consistently upregulated in sorafenib-resistant HCC models and associated with poor patient prognosis. Silencing YEATS2 significantly restored sorafenib sensitivity under TGF-beta1-conditioned settings. Mechanistically, YEATS2 physically interacted with TGF-beta-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), as supported by structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulation, and reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation. YEATS2 enhanced TAK1 activation and downstream stress-response signaling, whereas pharmacological or genetic inhibition of TAK1 abrogated YEATS2-mediated adaptive resistance to sorafenib. Our findings identify YEATS2 as a critical mediator of TGF-beta1-driven adaptive resistance to sorafenib in HCC through functional activation of TAK1 signaling. Our findings identify the YEATS2-TAK1 axis as a mechanistically relevant pathway underlying TGF-beta1-conditioned adaptive resistance to sorafenib in HCC.
abstract_zh: 尽管索拉非尼（Sorafenib）能有效延长肝细胞癌（HCC）患者的中位生存时间且副作用有限，但可能导致许多患者产生耐药性，成为延长HCC患者总生存期的障碍。我们先前的研究探讨了TGF-beta1通路在肝癌发生发展中的机制；TGF-beta1通路在索拉非尼耐药中的机制需进一步探索。通过对GEO数据库中TGF-beta1处理的Huh7细胞和索拉非尼耐药Huh7细胞相关测序结果的分析，我们鉴定出YEATS2为TGF-beta1响应基因，在索拉非尼耐药的HCC模型中持续上调，并与患者不良预后相关。沉默YEATS2在TGF-beta1条件设定下显著恢复索拉非尼敏感性。机制上，YEATS2与TGF-beta激活激酶1（TAK1）发生物理相互作用，这得到结构建模、分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟和相互共免疫沉淀的支持。YEATS2增强TAK1激活及下游应激反应信号，而TAK1的药理学或遗传学抑制则消除YEATS2介导的索拉非尼适应性耐药。我们的发现将YEATS2鉴定为TGF-beta1驱动的HCC中索拉非尼适应性耐药的关键介导因子，通过功能性激活TAK1信号实现。我们的发现将YEATS2-TAK1轴确定为TGF-beta1条件设定下HCC中索拉非尼适应性耐药的机制相关通路。
